artifact_policy: Retain selected row indices and domain-separated context hashes, token counts, optimizer/seed metadata, all fixed-horizon adapters, held-out per-prompt preference metrics, KL, input hashes, resource records, protocol/runner/auditor snapshots, and a SHA-256 manifest. Never write raw prompts, chosen/rejected text, token IDs, hidden features, or full model weights. Adapter files contain only the low-rank update.
claim_boundary: A development pass is only a candidate. The task outcome is preference agreement on disjoint human-labeled HH helpful-base prompts from the official training split, not downstream assistant task success. This is offline DPO, not online RL, and does not establish general alignment, safety, capability, external reproduction, or scale.

compute_limits.device: CPU only; CUDA, MPS, and accelerator placement are forbidden
compute_limits.network: disabled during formal run; HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1, HF_DATASETS_OFFLINE=1, TRANSFORMERS_OFFLINE=1, local_files_only=true

dataset.eligibility: Use the exact pinned fast tokenizer with add_special_tokens=true, no chat template, no truncation, and offset mappings. Require byte-identical contexts through the final `\n\nAssistant:` marker; nonempty chosen and rejected responses; both full transcript lengths <=1024; and at least one response token each. Add one EOS target after each response during sequence scoring. Invalid rows do not reserve a context.
dataset.leakage_boundary: The official HH helpful-base test split has been read in prior reward-model studies and is not used here. Development rows are disjoint prompts from the official train split, and therefore not an official test-set confirmation. HH source data and model training data are public; pretraining exposure cannot be excluded. The HH pair labels reflect human preferences between assistant responses, with the source collection process and limitations described in the pinned Anthropic data release.
dataset.license: MIT (as stated by the pinned dataset card)

selection.algorithm: For each eligible nonexcluded unique context, compute SHA256(domain || UTF8(context)), where domain is `vare-hh-human-dpo-development-v1\0`; sort by digest bytes, then context bytes. Use ranks [0,128) for the common training cohort and [128,384) for development. No labels, model scores, or response features may affect ranking. Preserve the exact source index and context hash inventory in the bundle.
selection.prompt_deduplication: one selected pair per exact byte-identical final assistant prompt context

dataset.source_hashing_rule: Hash the complete pinned train and test compressed containers as opaque bytes for provenance. Only parse the helpful-base train split. No HH test rows are read.

learner.adapter: Rank-16 residual on frozen final-layer hidden features for the full LM vocabulary. Transformer and original output-head weights are frozen. This is a custom CPU learner, not PEFT/TRL.
learner.checkpointing: No dev checkpoint selection; both arms train for exactly two epochs, fixed before dev scoring.
learner.comparison: Both methods use the same 128 human preference pairs, same context split, same adapter architecture, same optimizer settings and same three seeds.
learner.initialization: A sampled from N(0,1/sqrt(hidden_size)) with a CPU torch.Generator seeded per run; B initialized to zero.
learner.objective_dpo: Sequence-level DPO with beta 0.1 on human-labeled chosen/rejected responses, using the exact frozen base policy as reference.
learner.objective_sft: Chosen-only token-mean negative log likelihood on the same human-preferred response text; rejected responses are not trained on.
learner.response_token_features: For each response target token, use the frozen causal hidden state immediately preceding it; append EOS as an additional target. Preserve the exact raw HH transcript and do not add a chat template.
learner.row_order: For each seed, shuffle the fixed 128 source-ranked training pairs per epoch with Python random.Random(seed+99000).
learner.update_budget: One optimizer update per pair per epoch; pair microbatch 1.

bootstrap.interval: paired percentile 95% interval, averaging per-prompt outcomes across the three fixed seeds before resampling

development_gate.selection: No model/checkpoint selection; use the fixed two-epoch result. Report all gates. A pass advances only to a new confirmation protocol.

metrics.limitations: The human preference labels are the observed target, not an independent task-success or user-utility measure. Evaluation contexts are from the official training split but hash-disjoint from training and pilot contexts. Aggregate pairwise outcomes do not test free-form helpfulness, safety, or reasoning.
metrics.primary: Raw policy preference accuracy: for each human-labeled pair, predict chosen when sum-token log P(chosen|context) exceeds sum-token log P(rejected|context); ties score 0.5. Average by seed, then average seeds per prompt before prompt-cluster bootstrap.
metrics.primary_comparison: DPO minus frozen base pair accuracy on the same 256 development prompts. Also compare DPO with matched chosen-only SFT.
secondary: paired preference logistic NLL from raw sequence-sum margins
mean full-vocabulary token KL(policy || frozen base) over chosen and rejected response-token prediction contexts
response token counts and chosen/rejected length-only preference baseline

purpose: Revise the v1 CPU feasibility implementation to compute full-vocabulary sequence log probabilities in bounded token chunks after the locked v1 attempt exceeded the RSS guard before any held-out metrics were computed. The scientific task, cohort selection, optimizer, seeds, and advancement rule are unchanged.
